:::{#thm-norm-sum-square}
#### The squared norm of a sum

For any $\vecf{x}, \vecf{y} \in \reals^p$,

$$
\norm{\vecf{x} + \vecf{y}}^2
= \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 + 2\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}) + \norm{\vecf{y}}^2.
$$

In particular, if $\vecf{x} \perp \vecf{y}$ (@def-orthogonal-vectors), then
$\norm{\vecf{x} + \vecf{y}}^2 = \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 + \norm{\vecf{y}}^2$
(the **Pythagorean theorem**).

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\norm{\vecf{x} + \vecf{y}}^2
&= (\vecf{x} + \vecf{y}) \cdot (\vecf{x} + \vecf{y})
&& \text{(square both sides of @eq-l2-norm)}
\\
&= \vecf{x} \cdot (\vecf{x} + \vecf{y}) + \vecf{y} \cdot (\vecf{x} + \vecf{y})
&& \text{(@thm-dot-linear, first slot, } a \text{ and } b \text{ both equal to } 1 \text{)}
\\
&= \vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{x} + \vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y} + \vecf{y} \cdot \vecf{x} + \vecf{y} \cdot \vecf{y}
&& \text{(@thm-dot-linear, second slot, } a \text{ and } b \text{ both equal to } 1 \text{, twice)}
\\
&= \vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{x} + \vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y} + \vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y} + \vecf{y} \cdot \vecf{y}
&& \text{(@thm-lincom-symmetric)}
\\
&= \vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{x} + 2\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}) + \vecf{y} \cdot \vecf{y}
&& \text{(combine like terms)}
\\
&= \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 + 2\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}) + \norm{\vecf{y}}^2.
&& \text{(@eq-l2-norm, squared)}
\ea
$$

If $\vecf{x} \perp \vecf{y}$, then $\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y} = 0$,
and the middle term drops out.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-norm-sum-square}
#### Checking the expansion

For $\vecf{x} = (3, 0)$ and $\vecf{y} = (1, 4)$:
$\vecf{x} + \vecf{y} = (4, 4)$, so $\norm{\vecf{x} + \vecf{y}}^2 = 16 + 16 = 32$,
and $\norm{\vecf{x}}^2 + 2\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}) + \norm{\vecf{y}}^2
= 9 + 2 \cd 3 + 17 = 32$.
For the orthogonal vectors $(3, 0)$ and $(0, 4)$,
$\norm{(3, 4)}^2 = 25 = 9 + 16$, the $3$-$4$-$5$ right triangle.

:::
